test.name: Verify confidence calibration on the death-certificate person link
test.description: Review pe_005, the person_evidence link from a_013 (death certificate naming Thomas Flynn as Patrick's father) to person I1 (Patrick Flynn). The link is `confident` — the death certificate names Patrick Flynn, Schuylkill County, 1908, matching the subject's known identity. The skill should confirm the confidence calibration is appropriate.

input.delegation:
Review the person_evidence link pe_005 (from a_013, the death certificate, to Patrick Flynn) and assess whether its confidence calibration is justified.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should confirm `confidence: "confident"` is appropriate — the death certificate directly names 'Patrick Flynn' of Schuylkill County 1908, matching the subject's known place and time of death with no plausible alternative candidates

Should evaluate whether the existing `rationale` cites multiple matching attributes (name, place, date) and addresses why competing candidates were ruled out — not just 'names match'. Grade whether the REVIEW identifies those gaps; the stored rationale was written by the fixture, not by the agent, so its own quality is never scored against the agent.

This is a review. Not persisting a change is correct in a review and is not penalized, including proposing an edit to pe_005 and asking for authorization (test_pe005_unchanged_when_review_confirms requires pe_005 unchanged). Grade the content of any proposed change against item 0 as usual.

The death certificate's Pennsylvania birthplace (a_012) against the censuses' Ireland is conflict c_001, and c_001 is RESOLVED: Ireland accepted, the certificate's entry rejected as the son-in-law informant's likely error. A resolved conflict is not an open contradiction, so it does not cap this link. A review that downgrades pe_005 on that ground is a calibration error, not a correct downgrade (genealogist ruling, 2026-09-29). Naming c_001 and explaining why it does not reduce the tier is good work.
